edge_threshold.method: Smallest claimed edge t (0-30% in 1% steps) such that past bets claiming t to t+5% returned more than 0 per unit staked at the 95% lower bound, and so did every higher band with at least 30 bets; ranges resample whole matches; found on development seasons, then checked on the latest season (bets at t and up must have returned more than 0).
edge_threshold.note: No minimum edge works. At every claimed edge from 0% to 30%, the 739 past player bets lost money or could plausibly have lost it, so no edge the model claims is large enough to trust. The best band was 13%-18%: 82 bets returned +25.9% a bet (range -61.9% to +145.4%).

lean.title: Blend Lean replayed on Pinnacle's early prices
lean.note: Blend Lean replayed on Pinnacle's early prices from football-data, not on DraftKings: each league's blend refitted every 28 days on earlier matches only, sigma from each fit's own matches, $1 a bet on the side at least 1 sigma above the early price's break-even, CLV against Pinnacle's margin-free close. Pinnacle is a sharper price than DraftKings, so this is a tougher test than the live one, and it isn't the live book: a blend fitted on Pinnacle and fed Pinnacle's own prices doesn't have the mismatch live Lean has (fitted on Pinnacle, fed DraftKings' price, with b above 1 sharpening it). The Champions League has no early prices: it is replayed at DraftKings' close and kept out of the pooled numbers.

rule.blend_fit: Pinnacle's margin-free close beside the model's walk-forward chance
rule.clv: entry odds x Pinnacle's margin-free (Shin) close - 1
rule.cup: Champions League at DraftKings' bought close (cup_backtest.py), CLV against Pinnacle's close at the same moment; kept out of `all`
rule.driver: market = still at least 1 sigma with the model's term taken out of the fitted blend (c = 0, a and b kept as fitted, no refit); model = only with it
rule.driver_note: Market-driven: the pick still clears 1 sigma when the model's term is taken out of the fitted blend (the blend's other weights are kept as fitted, not refitted). Model-driven: it clears 1 sigma only with the model's term in. The model's term compares the model's chances across home, draw and away, not against the price, so where the model's weight is positive it lifts the outcome the model rates highest relative to the others, even when the model rates that outcome below the market.

bands.edge_from: p_bet x odds - 1 (the blend's edge); z beside it
bands.note: Every bet, split by its decimal odds (lo < odds <= hi), by the edge the strategy claimed when it bet, and by its CLV; the edge and CLV bands are cut at the pooled domestic leagues' quintiles, the same cuts in every league. ROI and CLV are per $1 with 95% ranges from resampling matches. If the model had skill, CLV would rise with the claimed edge.

calibration.note: Every outcome (home, draw, away) of every scored match, not only the bets: the model's raw walk-forward chance, the blend and the price (margin-free), each against what happened; `bets` is the strategy's own picks (predicted vs 1/odds vs won). Each bin holds the rows whose predicted chance falls in it: predicted is their average chance, implied the price's, realized how often they won (95% range). On a well-calibrated model realized sits on predicted. The slope is from logit(won) = a + b x logit(predicted): below 1 the chances are too spread out (over-confident).

flat.note: Tracked alternative only: the same trades with a different stake, no new bets; flat $10 stays the record. Paper bankroll $1,000 at the first trade; quarter Kelly (0.25 x f*, f* = (p x odds - 1) / (odds - 1)), at most 5% of the bankroll a bet, nothing when f* <= 0. Each stake uses only the bankroll from bets settled before it opened; pushes and voids return the stake. Kelly assumes p is right: every strategy's CLV is below 0, so the edge it sizes on is not proven.

match.name: Match model (Dixon-Coles)
equation: home goals ~ Poisson(lambda), lambda = exp(intercept + home_adv + attack[home] + defence[away])
away goals ~ Poisson(mu), mu = exp(intercept + attack[away] + defence[home])
P(home x, away y) = tau(x, y) x Poisson(x; lambda) x Poisson(y; mu), with tau(0,0) = 1 - lambda mu rho, tau(0,1) = 1 + lambda rho, tau(1,0) = 1 + mu rho, tau(1,1) = 1 - rho, else 1
fitted by weighted likelihood: each match weighted exp(-xi x age in days); the goals are (1 - xg_weight) x goals + xg_weight x xG

terms.intercept: the league's baseline scoring rate (log goals a game)
terms.home_adv: the home side's extra log goals (dropped at a neutral venue)
terms.attack / defence: each team's log rating: attack raises its own goals, defence raises its opponent's (higher = a weaker defence); each sums to 0 over the league
terms.rho: Dixon-Coles' correction for 0-0, 1-0, 0-1 and 1-1, which plain Poisson gets slightly wrong; rho < 0 makes 0-0 and 1-1 a little likelier
terms.xi: time weight per day; half_life_days is how old a match is when it counts half as much
terms.xg_weight: how much of each match's goals come from Understat's xG instead of the score (0 = goals only, where Understat doesn't cover the league)
terms.ridge: a penalty pulling ratings toward 0 (only the Champions League's cross-league fit uses it, so a club with few matches stays sensible)

match.note: The home, draw and away chances are the sums of P(home x, away y) over the score grid. The Champions League is one fit over every football-data league the cup's clubs play in plus the European results (goals only).

blend.name: Blend Lean (blend of price and model)
equation: score_k = a_k + b x log(price_k) + c x log(model_k), for k = home, draw, away (a_home = 0)
z_k = (p_bet_k - 1/odds_k) / sigma; a Lean pick at z >= 1, Strong at z >= 2
a Lean trade opens only when 1.50 < odds_k <= 3.00 (since 24 Oct); a pick outside it opens none

terms.price_k: the bookmaker's margin-free chance (Shin): Pinnacle's close when the blend is fitted, DraftKings' price when it is used live
terms.a_draw, a_away: fixed tilts toward the draw and the away side
terms.b: the weight on the price: above 1 sharpens it (favourites up, long shots down), below 1 flattens it
terms.c: the weight on the model: 0 ignores it; only its relative size across home, draw and away matters
terms.sigma: how far the blend usually strays from the price in this competition (sd of blend - price on the fit's matches)
terms.odds range: decimal 1.50 to 3.00 (-200 to +200), the owner's cut of 24 Oct: the shortest and longest prices are left out

blend.note: Fitted per league on every earlier match with Pinnacle's close; the live fit is in match_blends.json. A pick is market-driven when it still reaches 1 sigma with c set to 0.
blend.odds_range_note: Since 24 Oct, Blend Lean only trades between -200 and +200 (decimal 1.50 to 3.00): owner's decision after the first 15 settled trades. Picks outside the range open no trade; the old rule (all odds) is tracked beside it as a shadow.

corners_f.name: Team corners model (f)
equation: home corners ~ NB2(mean_h, alpha_home), mean_h = mean_home x for[home] x against[away]
away corners ~ NB2(mean_a, alpha_away), mean_a = mean_away x for[away] x against[home]
for[t] = (sum of t's corners / league mean + k_for) / (matches + k_for); against[t] likewise with k_against
NB2: variance = mean + alpha x mean^2

terms.mean_home / mean_away: the league's average corners for the home and away side over the fit window
terms.for[t] / against[t]: how many corners a team takes / concedes as a ratio to the league average (1 = average)
terms.k_for / k_against: empirical-Bayes pseudo-matches pulling each ratio toward 1: a team needs about k matches before its own record counts half
terms.alpha: NB2 dispersion: how much more spread out corner counts are than Poisson

corners_f.note: Fitted per league on the 730 days of football-data corner counts before today; an over at line L wins when the team's corners exceed L.

comeback_research.title: Favourites coming back from behind
comeback_research.question: When the favourite is losing at half-time, does backing it at the in-play price make money?
comeback_research.rule: $1 on the favourite trailing at half-time, at DraftKings' in-play price from the snapshot at kickoff + 55 min.
comeback_research.verdict_text: No. On 732 bets the in-play price paid out less than the stakes: ROI -25.1% (-38.3% to -10.2%). The market already rates these comebacks higher than they happen.

C.label: Design C: eight leagues, 2022/23 to 2024/25 (without B's matches)

phase1.note: Free data, 2017/18 to 2024/25. Favourites who fall behind won more often than a simple model that ignores the score and spreads goals evenly over 90 minutes. About a third of the half-time gap is just that second halves have more goals. This compared against a model, not against any price.

timelines.note: Free ESPN goal timelines, eight leagues, 2017/18 to 2024/25. When the underdog scores first, the favourite beats the score-blind model by a similar 3 to 6 points whatever the minute, so no minute stands out. Testing it at real prices would need about 1,882 snapshots (18,820 credits); not bought.

notes: The price is DraftKings' in-play moneyline on the favourite, taken from the odds archive's snapshot about 55 minutes after kickoff, inside the half-time break. Only quotes updated after kickoff and at most 5 minutes old count.

Phase 1 found favourites come back more often than a simple model says. The market already knows: at half-time it priced the comeback at 21.3% while 17.0% happened (design C), so backing the trailing favourite lost about a quarter of the stake.
Design B's positive season (+7.3%) was not a pattern. C, on prices never seen before, lost 25.1%, and every by-league, by-season and by-band line here is descriptive.

A new idea from these numbers, laying the trailing favourite included, needs its own pre-registration on seasons not used here (2025/26 or later) and the owner's approval before any credits are spent.
